biography: Margaret Boden was a British philosopher, psychologist, and artificial-intelligence researcher whose work clarified what creativity involves and how computational systems might participate in it. She distinguished combinational, exploratory, and transformational creativity, while insisting that novelty alone is not enough: creative work also has to matter within a field of value and judgment. Her framework lets PHIL 123 distinguish the generation of surprising outputs from authorship, evaluation, skill, and responsible innovation.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Boden gives students a precise vocabulary for comparing kinds of creativity without equating novelty, generation, authorship, and value.
